independent_computation.method: The leaf is a single post-mitigation damage event, and the scenario inputs (champions, levels, ranks) are not in the permitted evidence tree. What IS independently checkable is the multiplicative factor between the two values, because both game rules named by the scenario (Black Cleaver 'Carve', Bloodsong 'Expose Weakness') are pure multipliers on any damage event against the debuffed target. So I tested the observed factor against every factor derivable from the cached wiki text.

observed_factor.band_note: both leaves are printed to 1 dp, so the true factor lies in [109.75/94.15, 109.85/94.05]

rules_instantiated.carve_shred: target armor A -> A x (1 - 0.06 x stacks), 5 stacks max = 30% [data/items.json id 3071, passive 'Carve']
rules_instantiated.expose_weakness: target takes +8% (melee holder) / +5% (ranged holder) damage from ALL sources [data/items.json id 3877, passive 'Spellblade']
rules_instantiated.amp_composition: percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction [data/wiki-atoms/damage.json damage.modifier]

exact_fit_found.statement: The observed factor is exactly 7/6, and 7/6 is exactly what the two cached wiki rules produce against a 50-armor target with a ranged Bloodsong holder.
work: predicted new = 94.1 x 7/6 = 109.7833 -> prints as 109.8   (matches the new value)
predicted old (neither target debuff shared into this pair's damage) = 109.7833 x 6/7 = 94.1   (matches the old value)
exact_fit_found.why_this_is_the_correct_direction: Both effects are TARGET-side debuffs in the cached wiki text, not attacker-local buffs. Carve is 'applies a stack of Carve' to the enemy and 'inflicts 6% armor reduction' on that enemy; Expose Weakness explicitly causes the target 'to take X% increased damage from all sources'. In a roster/coupled fight, every participant hitting that debuffed target must see both. An engine that priced this pair's damage without them understates the event by exactly the 7/6 measured here.

independent_computation.limits_of_this_check: The scenario's participant list, levels, ranks and target armor are defined outside the permitted evidence tree (scripts/), so I could not recompute the absolute event damage from first principles - only the factor between the two values. The factor test is still discriminating: it is satisfied exactly by the two wiki-sourced target debuffs the scenario is named after and by no competing reading that leaves the old value correct.

sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

Death's Dance 'Ignore Pain': Reduces {{rd|30%|10%}} of all post-mitigation physical and magic damage received; Ravenous Hydra 'Cleave': {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}} - in both cases the first slot is the known melee value, so Expose Weakness is 8% melee / 5% ranged.

Independent damage value modifiers distinct from resistances: percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.
Armor and magic resistance reduce incoming physical/magic damage by a percentage (actual = raw x 100/(100 + resistance)); negative resistances amplify damage.

the established model uses a fixed 0.8 x max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch) ... the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +/-20% at the extremes ... Recommendation: replace the constant with the closed-form Cesaro mean when a champion module needs exact BC numbers

asides: The measured factor rules OUT additive merging of percent amps (would have printed 109.2), which is the behavior the cached wiki rule forbids - a useful positive signal about the new engine independent of this leaf's verdict.

The diff is consistent with Black Cleaver at the full 5-stack 30% shred, not the 0.8 x max_stacks (24%) constant documented in math-foundations Sec 2.3. If that constant is still live elsewhere in the engine, this scenario and that model now disagree.
